collection_method: Read-only GitHub issue-search, issue and comment GET requests through the GitHub connector. Embedded code and reproductions were treated as evidence and were not executed. No packages, agents, bots, tools, MCP servers, Telegram services, target systems, attachments or linked demonstrations were run or contacted.

selected_records.title: .NET: [Bug]: HandoffAgentExecutor resumes an approved tool call against the wrong participant (the entry-point agent, not the one that raised it)
selected_records.provider_attribution: Microsoft Agent Framework configured workflow; no provider execution established.
selected_records.assessment: The reporter initially described an approval response resuming against the entry agent instead of the worker. Project triage could not reproduce the wrong-recipient behavior in a provider-free two-call test, and the reporter closed the issue to investigate a different topology. Retained as an unresolved routing lead, not a verified exchange.

selected_records.title: Python: always_require tool approval silently bypassed when preceded by a declaration-only or unknown call in the same batch
selected_records.provider_attribution: Microsoft Agent Framework Python function loop; no model-provider attribution.
selected_records.assessment: Project automation and contributors reproduced order-dependent batch classification that could suppress an always-require approval. A maintainer recorded a fix with order-invariance and no-execution-before-resolution tests. This is a single-agent tool authorization control, not an inter-agent task-result exchange.

selected_records.title: Python: [Bug]: Functional workflow checkpoint replay can swap cached results between concurrent calls to the same @step
selected_records.provider_attribution: Microsoft Agent Framework Functional Workflow replay; no model-provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: A deterministic local reproduction and automated project triage show checkpoint replay swapping cached results between concurrent logical branches that call the same step. The replayed branches consume each other's prior results. The reporter explicitly classifies this as ordinary functional correctness; branches are configured workflow paths rather than independently authenticated agents.

selected_records.title: Python: [Bug]: Telegram samples execute commands addressed to other bots
selected_records.provider_attribution: Microsoft Agent Framework Telegram hosting samples; no live Telegram or model execution.
selected_records.assessment: A parser-level test showed a command addressed to another bot could be accepted locally. Project automation reproduced the parsing defect, but the reporter explicitly avoided a live group test. This is wrong-recipient command routing without an observed task-result transfer or live action.

selected_records.title: MCPServerStreamableHTTP: concurrent callers can leak per-request auth headers across each other
selected_records.provider_attribution: PydanticAI MCP client lifecycle; no MCP server or model-provider execution established.
selected_records.assessment: The original class had already been removed when reported, but a maintainer said the replacement MCPToolset retained the same overlapping-lifecycle issue and documented the limitation. No live cross-tenant request or task-result exchange was supplied.

selected_records.title: Duplicate tool_call_id silently mis-binds tool execution (last call wins for every slot)
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled wrong-tool execution and audit-history corruption
selected_records.provider_attribution: PydanticAI tool execution; no provider attribution beyond malformed model output.
selected_records.assessment: A deterministic reproduction shows duplicate tool-call identifiers causing the later tool to execute twice while history retains misleading call/return associations. The project accepted implementation work. This is a single-agent tool-dispatch defect, not a result exchange between distinct participants.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. The strongest exchange-shaped control is deterministic wrong-branch cached-result use during configured workflow replay; the only apparent wrong-participant handoff was not reproduced and was withdrawn for further investigation.
limitations: Searches were capped at 30 newest-updated rows and overlap; this is not a complete issue census.
Issue bodies and comments are public assertions and controlled reproductions, not authenticated agent telemetry.
Configured branches, tools and bot parsers are not independently verified autonomous participants.
Closed or reproduced tracker labels establish project state, not rogue intent or continuing autonomous activity.
No embedded code, package, reproduction, bot, tool, MCP server, agent runtime or external service was executed or contacted.

Advancement requires an unpublished original exchange with independently corroborated autonomous participants, transferred task work actually used by a distinguishable recipient, and evidence that the coordination itself crossed operator authorization in a real run.
redactions: No credentials, authentication headers, executable reproduction bodies, private logs, personal addresses or live bot identifiers are included.
Assessments retain public record links, timestamps and body hashes while summarizing mechanisms at a domain level.
